title: A DAG whose names are out of order
notes: C>B means C has to come before B, even though B comes first alphabetically. A is the only vertex with in-degree 0, so it goes first. Removing A's arcs frees C, removing C's frees B, and so on: A, C, B, E, D, F, G.
ops: A>B, A>C, B>D, B>E, C>B, C>D, D>G, E>D, E>F, F>G
